headline: High: shared filesystem/git and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and conflicting edits between Gemini CLI and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, while Mentat reads selected files and writes diffs. Because both share files and git state, content from one can be consumed by the other as trusted input. This is not provably blocked, though it is less direct than a clipboard bridge.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree or git branch, injected instructions in files can influence the other agent.
IF Gemini CLI is configured to read MCP/file content as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable MCP for Gemini CLI unless needed.
Review file diffs before handing outputs from one agent to the other.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access, and both touch source code or files in the cwd. In a shared workspace, sensitive file contents can flow into either agent’s model backend and then out over network calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF the same directory contains secrets or regulated data, both agents can ingest it.
IF either agent sends file contents to its provider by default, those contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate service accounts and API keys.
Restrict network egress during sensitive tasks.
Pass only minimal file subsets to Mentat.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data classification controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and both share state via filesystem. That creates a direct race on the same repo or branch, with conflicting edits and history rewrites possible without any locking shown in either profile. The overlap is dangerous in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository concurrently, their writes can overwrite each other.
IF either agent commits or rebases without external locking, git state can diverge or be lost.
mitigations: Run only one agent per repo at a time.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Require manual review before git commits.
Lock the workspace during edits.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or file-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce tool-using outputs and Mentat can turn file-based suggestions into diffs. If Mentat treats Gemini’s output as authoritative, an error can cascade into incorrect edits. The profiles do not show a verification step between them, so the pathway exists but is not maximally severe.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Gemini CLI output without independent verification, mistakes propagate into edits.
IF Gemini CLI emits malformed or misleading instructions, Mentat may apply them as diffs.
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents.
Compare outputs against source files before applying diffs.
Use structured templates for handoff text.
Limit Gemini CLI to analysis-only mode for handoffs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation on inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or retention mismatch documented. The main compliance concern is that both can touch source code and send data to external model providers, but the profiles do not show a specific regulatory conflict. I therefore keep this low rather than infer a stronger mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, external API calls may create policy obligations.
IF an operator requires strict local-only processing, either agent would violate that requirement when configured with remote models.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the workspace.
Use local-only models where available.
Review retention settings for both providers.
Document data handling expectations for the repo.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
